"We used to say build the MVP. Now you should build the system that builds the MVP first."

Here's my new episode with @ryancarson where he shared how he runs his startup solo with AI agents:

✅ OpenClaw as his AI chief of staff to triage emails, book meetings, and do sales outreach

today_focus.title: CEOs are uniquely prone to AI psychosis because they’re sufficiently distant from the last mile of work that still has to happen to generate most value with AI.
today_focus.brief: CEOs are uniquely prone to AI psychosis because they’re sufficiently distant from the last mile of work that still has to happen to generate most value with AI。它反映的是一线 builder 对产品和工作流变化的即时反馈，价值在于捕捉正式新闻之前的使用趋势。
today_focus.social_original_text:
CEOs are uniquely prone to AI psychosis because they’re sufficiently distant from the last mile of work that still has to happen to generate most value with AI.

So when they play with AI, they see the happy path results, often not considering the next 10 or 20 things that have to happen to get sustainable results from agents.

“Look I made this awesome product prototype”. Yes but you didn’t have to review the code before it went into production and fix a bunch of issues.

“Look I generated a contract”. Yes but you didn’t verify all the terms before it goes out to the counterparty and didn’t have to wire up all the past contracts to work with.

The best thing you can do as a CEO is to use AI a *ton* to figure out the real implications of agents in the enterprise, and come out the other side with an appreciation for both the upside and the real work that goes into them.
today_focus.translation_zh: CEO们尤其容易陷入AI狂热，因为他们离真正释放AI价值所必需的“最后一公里”工作相去甚远。 因此，当他们试用AI时，往往只看到理想路径下的结果，却很少考虑要让智能体产出可持续的成果，后续还需完成十几二十项工作。 “看，我做出了超棒的产品原型。”没错，但你无需在代码投产前进行审查，也无需修复一堆漏洞。 “看，我生成了一份合同。”没错，但你无需在发给合作方前核实所有条款，也无需将其与所有历史合同进行系统对接。 作为CEO，最好的做法是大量使用AI，摸清智能体在企业落地的真实影响，最终既能看清其潜力，也能认清背后所需的扎实工作。
evidence_titles: CEOs are uniquely prone to AI psychosis because they’re sufficiently distant from the last mile of work that still has to happen to generate most value with AI.
evidence_summaries:
CEOs are uniquely prone to AI psychosis because they’re sufficiently distant from the last mile of work that still has to happen to generate most value with AI.

So when they play with AI, they see the happy path results, often not considering the next 10 or 20 things that have to happen to get sustainable results from agents.

“Look I made this awesome product prototype”. Yes but you didn’t have to review the code before it went into production and fix a bunch of issues.

“Look I generated a contract”. Yes but you didn’t verify all the terms before it goes out to the counterparty and didn’t have to wire up all the past contracts to work with.

The best thing you can do as a CEO is to use AI a *ton* to figure out the real implications of agents in the enterprise, and come out the other side with an appreciation for both the upside and the real work that goes into them.

industry_views.title: CEOs are uniquely prone to AI psychosis because they’re sufficiently distant from the last mile of work that still has to happen to generate most value with AI.
industry_views.brief: CEOs are uniquely prone to AI psychosis because they’re sufficiently distant from the last mile of work that still has to happen to generate most value with AI。它反映的是一线 builder 对产品和工作流变化的即时反馈，价值在于捕捉正式新闻之前的使用趋势。
industry_views.social_original_text:
CEOs are uniquely prone to AI psychosis because they’re sufficiently distant from the last mile of work that still has to happen to generate most value with AI.

So when they play with AI, they see the happy path results, often not considering the next 10 or 20 things that have to happen to get sustainable results from agents.

“Look I made this awesome product prototype”. Yes but you didn’t have to review the code before it went into production and fix a bunch of issues.

“Look I generated a contract”. Yes but you didn’t verify all the terms before it goes out to the counterparty and didn’t have to wire up all the past contracts to work with.

The best thing you can do as a CEO is to use AI a *ton* to figure out the real implications of agents in the enterprise, and come out the other side with an appreciation for both the upside and the real work that goes into them.
industry_views.translation_zh: CEO们尤其容易陷入AI狂热，因为他们离真正释放AI价值所必需的“最后一公里”工作相去甚远。 因此，当他们试用AI时，往往只看到理想路径下的结果，却很少考虑要让智能体产出可持续的成果，后续还需完成十几二十项工作。 “看，我做出了超棒的产品原型。”没错，但你无需在代码投产前进行审查，也无需修复一堆漏洞。 “看，我生成了一份合同。”没错，但你无需在发给合作方前核实所有条款，也无需将其与所有历史合同进行系统对接。 作为CEO，最好的做法是大量使用AI，摸清智能体在企业落地的真实影响，最终既能看清其潜力，也能认清背后所需的扎实工作。
evidence_titles: CEOs are uniquely prone to AI psychosis because they’re sufficiently distant from the last mile of work that still has to happen to generate most value with AI.
evidence_summaries:
CEOs are uniquely prone to AI psychosis because they’re sufficiently distant from the last mile of work that still has to happen to generate most value with AI.

So when they play with AI, they see the happy path results, often not considering the next 10 or 20 things that have to happen to get sustainable results from agents.

“Look I made this awesome product prototype”. Yes but you didn’t have to review the code before it went into production and fix a bunch of issues.

“Look I generated a contract”. Yes but you didn’t verify all the terms before it goes out to the counterparty and didn’t have to wire up all the past contracts to work with.

The best thing you can do as a CEO is to use AI a *ton* to figure out the real implications of agents in the enterprise, and come out the other side with an appreciation for both the upside and the real work that goes into them.

items.title: CEOs are uniquely prone to AI psychosis because they’re sufficiently distant from the last mile of work that still has to happen to generate most value with AI.
items.brief: CEOs are uniquely prone to AI psychosis because they’re sufficiently distant from the last mile of work that still has to happen to generate most value with AI。它反映的是一线 builder 对产品和工作流变化的即时反馈，价值在于捕捉正式新闻之前的使用趋势。
items.social_original_text:
CEOs are uniquely prone to AI psychosis because they’re sufficiently distant from the last mile of work that still has to happen to generate most value with AI.

So when they play with AI, they see the happy path results, often not considering the next 10 or 20 things that have to happen to get sustainable results from agents.

“Look I made this awesome product prototype”. Yes but you didn’t have to review the code before it went into production and fix a bunch of issues.

“Look I generated a contract”. Yes but you didn’t verify all the terms before it goes out to the counterparty and didn’t have to wire up all the past contracts to work with.

The best thing you can do as a CEO is to use AI a *ton* to figure out the real implications of agents in the enterprise, and come out the other side with an appreciation for both the upside and the real work that goes into them.
items.translation_zh: CEO们尤其容易陷入AI狂热，因为他们离真正释放AI价值所必需的“最后一公里”工作相去甚远。 因此，当他们试用AI时，往往只看到理想路径下的结果，却很少考虑要让智能体产出可持续的成果，后续还需完成十几二十项工作。 “看，我做出了超棒的产品原型。”没错，但你无需在代码投产前进行审查，也无需修复一堆漏洞。 “看，我生成了一份合同。”没错，但你无需在发给合作方前核实所有条款，也无需将其与所有历史合同进行系统对接。 作为CEO，最好的做法是大量使用AI，摸清智能体在企业落地的真实影响，最终既能看清其潜力，也能认清背后所需的扎实工作。
